notes.text:
HISTORICAL: superseded by the user-approved October 29 single-host Compose design.
Core deployment view. Each lab runs a complete independently versioned AI4R with its own research, factory and RSI. JiuwenSwarm provides native skills, tools/MCP, teams/workflows and evolution integration points; do not create a competing generic skill manager. CC is our deployable capability package/contract, not a claim that upstream Skills are OCI images. Use native skill discovery/invocation and scoped visibility, with thin adapters to pinned CC containers. Domain applications may be long-lived CC services and retain application state. The stable supervisor is an execution-control responsibility: reuse JiuwenBox where compatible, Docker for OCI ownership, and provider APIs for whole-VM stop. Model routing is available to both AI4R and container CCs. General/domain sources have different storage backends and feed selected versions into a lab. Lab-local factory output and upstream contributions are detailed on slide 5. No central research runtime controls every lab.
Upstream JiuwenSwarm 02b37f47fbefe80a58e4ed88606120818ca44ac3: agents/swarm/providers/skills.py, tools.py, evolution_rails.py; server/runtime/skill/skill_manager.py; docs/en/MCPConfiguration.md. Source reviewed, integration untested. https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/jiuwenswarm

Designs/Sandbox Lab Design.md, selected VM-per-lab and selective JiuwenBox reuse, October 27, 2026.
Composition clarification: Factory and research workflows reuse the same CC machinery. Factory is a purpose-specific bundle of CCs, potentially callable as a composite CC, not a new execution layer. Deployment boundaries follow actual dependencies/isolation needs. Independent qualification authority and stable host/provider controls remain explicit even where implementation uses CCs.
Labs produce research outputs as well as capabilities: reports, discoveries/findings and supporting evidence. Research/reporting CCs assemble these outputs within the recurring research workflow; reporting need not wait until the entire project ends. Preserve them in lab data and expose them through the lab interface or an authorized export. The output box denotes deliverables, not another service or automatic public publication. Findings feed knowledge and subsequent investigations. Reports state the evidence, methods and uncertainty, including useful negative/inconclusive outcomes. A candidate hypothesis or generated report is not automatically a validated discovery. Capability contribution/adoption remains a separate path. All this is proposed output behavior, not a measured discovery result.
CCs hold the AI4R agent capabilities: specialist instructions/skills, agent or workflow code, tool implementations, software dependencies and declared model requirements. They can represent one agent, several collaborating agents, a tool or a composite workflow. Research and Factory workflows compose these CCs through native JiuwenSwarm interfaces. The lab provides orchestration, state, scoped execution and model routes around them. Shared model weights remain outside the package unless a lab-private model profile explicitly includes them. A logical CC/bundle is not necessarily one dedicated process or container; deployment follows declared dependencies and isolation needs. This is the intended packaging architecture, not a newly verified runtime result.
Visual conventions: blue research/orchestration; violet CC packages/composition; cyan model access; green persistent state; amber execution/control; slate checks; rose research outputs. Solid arrows carry requests/results/control/data; dashed arrows show configuration, references, imports, contribution proposals or optional escalation. Arrowheads terminate on the indicated node boundary. Categories express responsibilities, not mandatory separate services.
Imported CC packages enter the AI4R selection/qualification responsibility before execution; the import edge no longer goes directly into running CCs. The source receipt and detailed factory slide retain the qualification requirements.
Open-source hunt recommendation, October 27, 2026. Concrete names are qualification candidates, not installed or measured integration results. Existing native JiuwenSwarm remains the agent/Skill/workflow/evolution surface. Use Docker SDK/API for OCI ownership and systemd for stable service lifecycle, with JiuwenBox for compatible tool execution. A systemd unit cgroup does not automatically own Docker-daemon containers; the adapter must stop/reconcile both. libvirt is a supported Linux KVM option; prefer the existing provider if available. cloud-init can bootstrap guests. Shared gateway: qualify LiteLLM with PostgreSQL for key management, vLLM or remote APIs for serving, and explicit experimental model constraints. Private models remain inside their lab and outside shared discovery. restic needs consistent application exports and an independent repository. Quarto is a reporting CC tool, not another permanent control service. MLflow is optional for run comparison/UI, initially lab-local.

HISTORICAL: superseded by the user-approved October 29 single-host Compose design.
Slide 7. This is a private model workload, not a change to the default shared-inference service. Fine-tuning can mutate lab-owned weight/checkpoint copies. No other sandbox may call the private endpoint or read its weights/checkpoints. Enforce lab-scoped network policy, bind addresses and authorization, not only a hostname convention. Do not register it with shared gateways or service discovery. Operator administration and explicit export are distinct from sandbox access. Any future sharing requires a separate explicit promotion decision; nothing automatically opens cross-lab access. A private experiment can still use authorized shared inference as an external tool, but that shared endpoint is not its private model.
The lab needs an allocated compute/device route. VM ownership alone does not give it a GPU. If the selected VM provider cannot expose the required accelerator, mark that profile unavailable until a separately qualified lab-exclusive execution binding is designed. Do not claim Spark guest GPU passthrough. Memory, storage, checkpoint staging and GPU reservations count against real capacity. Training jobs may need exclusivity to protect other labs and valid comparisons. No new training framework is selected by this diagram.

notes.text:
HISTORICAL: superseded by the user-approved October 29 single-host Compose design.
Slide 8. Pause stops dispatch; it does not mean compute is released. Supervisor cancellation requests termination, escalates within a configured bound, then verifies process/job status. Normal lab stop quiesces/cancels owned work, stops local services and preserves project data. Independent host/provider control can force-stop the VM if guest control hangs. Force power-off is not an application-consistent checkpoint. Reconcile incomplete work at restart; do not silently replay external effects. Separate explicit deletion decides data disposition. TTL/idle policies may not delete unique project state.
Persistent volume placement, independent backup destination and restoration are concrete deployment inputs. Backup consistency and old-writer fencing are necessary. A copied simulator volume does not recreate live physics state unless the application supports it. Shared inference remains available when one lab stops. Human guest administration may override protections; no claim of tamper-proof evidence against the lab owner.
https://libvirt.org/manpages/virsh.html ; shutdown and destroy/power-off are distinct from storage deletion. Provider support must be qualified.

notes.text:
HISTORICAL: superseded by the user-approved October 29 single-host Compose design.
Slide 9. The stack is concrete at the responsibility/interface level. Exact host/provider, image pins, GPU allocation and model server are deployment qualifications, not fabricated current installations. Reuse OpenJiuwen where it preserves our contracts. JiuwenBox handles compatible sandbox/tool operations and may inform lifecycle adapters; it is not the whole VM manager or generic OCI engine. Existing native interfaces guide compatibility tests. Keep AI4R-specific packages, artifact transfer, independent qualification and research revisions under our ownership. Coder is an optional later workspace-access evaluation, not the selected research control plane.
First demonstrator has recurring research with at least one material revision, concurrent independent work where supported, a package import/qualification/invocation, shared endpoint requests with per-lab limits, private model access denial from another lab, actual job stop and independent VM stop, then retained-state continuation. Controlled drivers are distinguished from autonomous decisions. Measure useful outcomes, restart cost, total model/checking cost, resources and isolation failures. No benchmark gain is assumed.
